BREAKING: The US unemployment rate has remained below 5.0% for 62 consecutive months, its 2nd-longest streak on record.

This trails only the 64-month stretch recorded during the 1960s and 1970s.

This is also 20 months longer than the 42-month streak that ended during the 2020 pandemic.

The current run began in September 2021, when the unemployment rate fell to 4.7%, from 5.1% in August 2021.

To put this into perspective, the unemployment rate has averaged 5.6% since the start of the century.

The US job market is still remarkably resilient.

BREAKING: The delinquency rate on multifamily Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) rose +5 basis points in October, to 8.1%, its highest since 2016.

This figure has more than quadrupled since 2024.

Furthermore, the delinquency rate on CMBS for offices jumped +17 basis points last month, to 12.3%, matching the all-time high set in January 2026.

To put this into perspective, this percentage peaked at ~10.8% in 2012, following the 2008 Financial Crisis.

The commercial real estate crisis is still worsening.

This was the week it felt like investors finally threw in the white towel on the AI trade.

The S&P 500 was down just 2.7% for the week, but it felt far worse. The real damage wasn't in the index. It was in the hedge fund world, where what looked like a capitulation moment triggered a cascade of forced selling across hedge funds, leveraged ETFs, and CTAs. The Nasdaq 100 (NDX/QQQ) finished down 5% for the week, with more than 100% of that decline occurring in just two hours on Thursday, between 8:30 and 10:30 a.m. New York time.

The magnitude of the deleveraging was extraordinary. Volatility spiked, put-call ratios reached extremes, trading volumes exploded, and hedge funds cut exposure at a historic pace. Hedge fund closure rumors went viral.

And I was buying into the panic.  

In this week's video, I explain why I would try and catch a falling knife and why I believe we're witnessing a market structure deleveraging event rather than a breakdown in AI fundamentals or the economy. I go through the data behind the forced selling, the factor signals I'm watching for exhaustion, and why the midterm results may have actually reduced the risk of an AI bubble.

I also explore the changing market structure, the emerging importance of factor rotations, and why declining liquidity headwinds could be a significant positive for AI, Bitcoin, and gold.

The AI revolution is a long-duration investment opportunity being traded in an increasingly short-duration market.

Investing is becoming a counterpuncher's game. The market structure has changed forever and hedge fund leverage has forever peaked.

CapEx in the US is skyrocketing:

The value of US nondefense capital goods shipments, excluding aircraft, jumped +11.6% YoY in September, reaching a record $86 billion.

This marks the fastest annual growth rate since July 2021.

Even more impressive, shipments have risen at a 3-month annualized rate of +16.5%, the strongest pace since 2011, excluding the pandemic recovery.

Since October 2024, shipments have increased by +$12 billion, or +16.5%.

Much of this momentum is being fueled by the AI investment boom.

Orders for computers, servers, storage devices, and related equipment have surged +27% YoY, the largest annual increase since January 1997.

The AI infrastructure buildout is beyond massive.

US mortgage demand is down to historic lows:

US purchase mortgage applications index fell -2% last week, to 131 points, its 2nd-lowest since January 2025.

This also marks the 6th-lowest weekly reading since 1995, down -32% since January.

As a result, US mortgage applications are now -50% below the pre-pandemic levels seen in 2019.

This comes as the 30Y fixed mortgage rate has risen +120 basis points since February, to 7.18%, near its highest since November 2023.

Rates have now been above 7.0% for 7 consecutive weeks.

The US housing market is frozen.

BREAKING: The Fed’s balance sheet expanded +$3 billion in the week ending November 4th, to $6.75 trillion, its 3rd-highest level since mid-March 2025.

Total assets have surged +$212 billion since the December 2025 low.

Over this period, Treasury holdings have risen +$390 billion, to $4.58 trillion, their highest since March 2024.

At the same time, holdings of Mortgage-Backed Securities have declined -$170 billion, to $1.88 trillion, their lowest since June 2020.

The Fed's balance sheet stands now +$2.99 trillion, or +80%, above pre-pandemic levels.

The Fed's balance sheet is growing again.

Thursday was a historic session in the US options market:

US put option trading volume on CBOE surged to a record 11.23 million contracts on Thursday.

This surpassed the previous all-time high of 10.22 million contracts set on April 4th, 2025.

As a result, the 20-day average of put option volume rose to ~7 million contracts, near its highest on record.

By comparison, the 20-day average oscillated around 4 million contracts in 2022.

8 of the 10 highest daily put option volume readings have occurred in 2026.

We are seeing unprecedented options activity right now.

It took 23 trading days for the S&P 500 to be down 5% from the Oct 6th ATH.

Sam found that most bear markets started with a quick move down 5% from ATHs. In fact, only one bear market ever (34% in late '60s/early '70) took longer than 23 trading days to hit down 5%.

Could this go into a full fledged bear market? Of course it could, but for now we don't expect that and this suggests don't panic just yet.
